prompt: Long bridges are built with small gaps, often covered by metal finger plates, at intervals along the road deck. What are those expansion joints for?

options.text: The gaps are drainage channels that let rainwater escape from the road surface
The deck expands in hot weather and contracts in cold; the gaps give it room to change length without buckling or cracking
The gaps separate sections built in different years, and serve no physical purpose now
The gaps let strong winds pass through the deck so the bridge is not pushed sideways

explanation: Most building materials expand when heated and contract when cooled. Over a long bridge deck those small changes add up to centimetres, so gaps at the ends let the deck lengthen safely on hot days instead of buckling or cracking.
